answer: Sybil resistance binds each agent identity to a verifier-approved remote attestation: its TEE must prove that authorized code is running with the expected MRENCLAVE and a hardware-backed key. Duplicating an enclave image in virtual machines cannot recreate that key, measurement, or genuine platform evidence, so cloned identities are rejected. Creating many valid identities therefore requires acquiring separate physical silicon, imposing a real cost across the vine, canyon, and horizon of the network.
